newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish BGZ, Russian banks in talks on joint bank.
newsitem.headline: Polish BGZ, Russian banks in talks on joint bank.

text.p: Poland's Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) is in talks with several large Russian banks on setting up a joint bank in Russia which would service trade between the two countries, BGZ's deputy president said.
Andrzej Szczepek told Reuters on Thursday BGZ also wanted several big Polish trading firms, which do business with Russia to take stakes in the bank. BGZ services such traders as Agros and Elektrim.
"We are in serious talks with Russian banks, of the top 20, on setting up a joint bank which would service trade between the two countries," Szczepek said.

He said the bank, in which the Polish side would like to have more than 50 percent, could emerge already in 1998, if BGZ manages to reach a planned 500 million zlotys ($166.4 million) gross profit in 1997, which would end its financial problems.
"If BGZ's 1997 results are in line with the plan we will reach a positive solvency ratio and the Polish central bank would then be likely to give its approval for such a venture," Szczepek said.

BGZ fell into financial problems after inheriting a bad debts portfolio from communist times. It was additionally deepened in the early years of Poland's transformation into a market economy after 1989.
Szczepek estimated the value of Polish trade with Russia at about $3 billion and expected it to rise to $4 billion this year.
"About 90 percent of this trade is now serviced by foreign banks, and we could take over some of that market," he said.
BGZ will open its representative office in Moscow in March.
